problems.source_says: No passage says who produced the 1-10 creativity evaluations of the idea lists. The only similarly worded evaluations, in Appendix C ('We obtained evaluations, ranging from 1 to 10, for each answer submitted by each subject'), are plotted on a 'Footwear Average Score' axis with ticks at 7, 8, and 9 and an intercept of about 7.55. That is the level of the GPT-4 composite (control mean 7.207), far above the human-graded composite (control mean 4.099). So automated_score (GPT-4 as judge) is at least as likely as expert raters, and the coded value has no textual support. The form marks the point unresolved but still codes expert_raters. The measure field has no 'not stated' code, so the record should flag the rater as unknown instead of asserting one.

problems.source_says: The codebook rule gives with_ai: GPT-4 was available when the note was written, and the form's own construct is usefulness, not diversity. Recommendation quality does not score the brand choice that has a correct answer. The paper reports it 'regardless of the correctness of their answer' (Table 6 cols 3-4, Figure 8), and the Appendix B rubric scores the proposed tactical actions, not whether the brand choice is right. Those actions are business ideas with many acceptable answers, and the task asks for them to be innovative and creative. Codebook section 1 counts business ideas judged on usefulness as ideation output. The form also codes the S1 composite, which includes analytic questions such as market segmentation, as with_ai. If S2-O1 is recoded, the record also lacks the Figure 8 arm means (control 5.95 vs AI 7.21, +21%, for correct answers and 5.33 vs 6.28, +18%, for incorrect ones) and the Table 6 cols (3)-(4) coefficients. The form lists this as an open question for Review 1.

confirmed: Every outcome is scored on submitted answers, and none is self-reported. Two human graders scored each answered question for S1-O1, GPT-4 scored each answer for S1-O2, each idea list got a 1-10 creativity evaluation for S1-O3, Universal Sentence Encoder embeddings of the question-1 ideas give S1-O4 and S1-O5, and human graders scored S2-O1 and S2-O2 (PDF p. 13, printed p. 9, fn. 6; PDF p. 53; PDF p. 52; PDF p. 19; PDF p. 41, Table 4 notes).

AI was available to both AI arms while they wrote the scored experimental-task answers, and the only no-AI task (the assessment task) came first. So ai_available_when_produced 'yes' and timing 'immediate' hold, and no after_ai outcome exists (PDF p. 11, printed p. 7; PDF p. 12, printed p. 8; PDF p. 44, Appendix A).

Question codes follow the rule for S1-O1 to S1-O4. S1-O4 is a diversity outcome with AI available, so across_people. S1-O1 to S1-O3 are not diversity, so with_ai. S1-O5 (AI output against human output) and S2-O2 (correctness of a brand choice with one right answer) take 'none' under the form-spec note on question (PDF pp. 52-53; PDF p. 18, printed p. 14).

S1-O4 compares different people, so diversity, not flexibility, is the right construct. Each idea's average inner product with all ideas of other subjects in the same condition is averaged over the subject's ideas into a subject-level 'between semantic similarity', so the unit is participant. Only question 1 is analyzed, with 512-dimensional USE embeddings (PDF p. 52, Appendix D; PDF p. 16, printed p. 12).

Figure 6 and Appendix D Figure 1 are the same density plot. Its dashed mean lines run, from least to most similar, Control, GPT + Overview, GPT Only, GPT No Humans, and no means, SEs, or tests are printed. So treatment_lower on the diversity scale, with the sign reversal stated, holds for both AI arms, and figure_only is right (PDF p. 36; PDF p. 53).

The Figure 6 notes call the measure 'Average Within-Subject Semantic Similarity' while Appendix D defines a between-subject measure, and the Appendix D text has the 'without ... than those without access' typo, as the form records (PDF p. 36; PDF p. 53).

S1-O3: the text pools both AI arms as 'subjects with access to ChatGPT', reports 'significantly higher quality', and prints no number. Construct overall_creativity, direction treatment_higher, unit participant, and statistics 'none' hold (PDF p. 53, Appendix D).

The S1-O1 and S1-O2 text values match: 42.5%, 38%, 18.6%, 16.8%, mean per-question effects 1.69 (46.6%) and 1.36 (20.2%), 108 regressions, and footnote 7 on GPT-4 as a lenient grader. The composite Quality is the paper's primary outcome, so paper_primary holds (PDF p. 14, printed p. 10; PDF p. 13, printed p. 9).
Figure 5 bar labels match: 4.05 vs 5.79 (+43%) and 5.20 vs 6.06 (+17%), for subjects in the AI conditions only (PDF p. 35; PDF p. 15, printed p. 11).

S2-O1 values match Table 6: GPT + Overview 1.475 (0.242) and 1.331 (0.233), GPT Only 1.046 (0.289) and 0.941 (0.265), F-test 0.098 and 0.112, control mean 5.856, N 372, and 105 and 267 in cols (3)-(4). The text gives 1.47 (25.1%) and 1.05 (17.9%) and names BCG consultants and business-school students as graders (PDF p. 43; PDF p. 19).

S2-O2 values match Table 4 col (1) and Figure 7: GPT + Overview -0.245 (0.054), GPT Only -0.139 (0.053), F-test 0.082, control mean 0.844, N 373, and 84.5%, 60.0%, and 70.6% correct. The paper calls correctness its primary metric (PDF p. 41; PDF p. 37; PDF p. 18).
Appendix C Figure 3 plots 'Footwear Average Score' on an axis with ticks at 7, 8, and 9, with an intercept of about 7.55 and a slope of about 1.21, as the form says (PDF p. 51).
The Appendix B rubric scores tactical actions (identified, aligned with strategy, implementation detail, business reasoning, profit impact) and has no novelty or creativity criterion (PDF pp. 47-48).

No other outcome bears on the three questions. Completion and timing (Tables 2, 3, and 5) are not quality or creativity scores, Appendix C retainment covers AI users only and is correlational, and Appendix E is qualitative (PDF pp. 39-40 and 42; PDF pp. 49-51; PDF pp. 55-58).
summary: Criterion 3 holds: two human graders scored every answered question of the S1 product task (Table 1, the paper's primary outcome), the Universal Sentence Encoder similarity of the question-1 shoe ideas compares different participants' output (Figure 6, Appendix D), GPT-4 was available while the AI arms produced both, and every number the form records matches the PDF. The coding is still refuted on details: S1-O3's expert_raters has no support and the similarly worded Appendix C ratings sit on the GPT-4 scale, S2-O1's question 'none' departs from the codebook rule for a usefulness rating of requested 'innovative' business actions, S1-O5 wrongly says no person in its contrast had AI help, the GPT + Overview vs GPT Only diversity contrast is missing, and smaller points concern Figure 5's unnamed grader, S2-O2's graders, and a second Table 1 in Appendix E.
